pulls.title: argsman, cli: Allow options after non-option arguments (GNU-style)
pulls.body:
Allow options to be specified after non-option arguments in `ParseParameters`, matching GNU option parsing conventions (`getopt_long` style). Currently in `master`, once the first non-dash argument was encountered, all subsequent arguments were collected verbatim into `m_command`. This meant `-rpcwallet` and similar options were silently ignored when placed after a command or its positional args. The same misspelled option before the command would be a clear error; after the command, it was silently treated as a positional argument — potentially triggering unintended RPC behaviour. **_With this change_**: - Valid options after a command are stored in `command_line_options` exactly as if they appeared before the command. - Unrecognized options after a command are always errors (no silent fallback to positional). - A `--` separator stops option processing; all subsequent arguments are treated as positional regardless of leading dashes. - `bitcoin-cli`'s `CommandLineRPC` is updated to derive its args vector from `gArgs.GetCommand()` rather than re-scanning raw `argv`. - `bitcoin-wallet` benefits automatically: options such as `-wallet` placed after a command are now parsed correctly instead of being rejected as unexpected positional arguments.
Before and after: options after a command are now recognized...
**`-rpcwallet` after the command and its positional args:** - Before (`master`) — `-rpcwallet` is silently ignored; request goes to the wrong wallet: ``` $ bitcoin-cli -regtest -datadir=/tmp/btc listtransactions -rpcwallet=nonExistent [ ] ``` - After — correctly routes to the named wallet and fails with the expected error: ``` $ bitcoin-cli -regtest -datadir=/tmp/btc listtransactions -rpcwallet=nonExistent error code: -18 error message: Requested wallet does not exist or is not loaded ``` --- **`getaddressinfo` with `-rpcwallet` appended:** - Before (`master`) — `-rpcwallet` becomes an extra positional arg; `getaddressinfo` errors with its usage string: ``` $ bitcoin-cli -regtest -datadir=/tmp/btc getaddressinfo bcrt1q... -rpcwallet=nonExistent error message: getaddressinfo "address" ... ``` - After — wallet is correctly selected: ``` $ bitcoin-cli -regtest -datadir=/tmp/btc getaddressinfo bcrt1q... -rpcwallet=nonExistent error code: -18 error message: Requested wallet does not exist or is not loaded ``` --- **Multi-wallet: `-rpcwallet` no longer needs to come before the command:** - Before (`master`): ``` $ bitcoin-cli -regtest -datadir=/tmp/btc listtransactions error code: -19 error message: ...specify the "-rpcwallet=" option before the command... ``` ``` $ bitcoin-cli -regtest -datadir=/tmp/btc listtransactions -rpcwallet=mywallet error code: -19 ← still fails; option after command was ignored error message: ...specify the "-rpcwallet=" option before the command... ``` - After: — error message updated: ``` $ bitcoin-cli -regtest -datadir=/tmp/btc listtransactions error code: -19 error message: ...specify the "-rpcwallet=" option before or after the command... ``` — command executed successfully: ``` $ bitcoin-cli -regtest -datadir=/tmp/btc listtransactions -rpcwallet=mywallet [ { "address": "bcrt1q...", "category": "immature", "amount": 50.00000000, ... } ] ```
Before and after: misspelled options and the -- separator...
**Misspelled option is now an error rather than a silent positional arg:** Before (`master`) — `-rpcwalllet ` (note triple-l) silently absorbed as the `label` positional arg: ``` $ bitcoin-cli -regtest -datadir=/tmp/btc listtransactions -rpcwalllet=foo { ... } ← result returned, -rpcwallet went unnoticed ``` After: ``` $ bitcoin-cli -regtest -datadir=/tmp/btc getblock -rpcwalllet=foo error: Invalid parameter -rpcwalllet ``` --- **`--` separator: pass a dash-prefixed string as a positional RPC argument:** ``` $ bitcoin-cli -regtest -datadir=/tmp/btc somecommand -- -not-an-option ``` Everything after `--` is treated as a positional argument, so `-not-an-option` is passed to the RPC unchanged.
Before and after: bitcoin-wallet commands...
**`-wallet` option placed after the command:** Before (`master`) — option treated as an unexpected positional arg: ``` $ bitcoin-wallet -regtest -datadir=/tmp/btc create -wallet=myWallet Error: Additional arguments provided (-wallet=myWallet). Methods do not take arguments. Please refer to -help. ``` After: ``` $ bitcoin-wallet -regtest -datadir=/tmp/btc create -wallet=myWallet Topping up keypool... Wallet info Name: myWallet Format: sqlite Descriptors: yes Encrypted: no HD (hd seed available): yes Keypool Size: 8000 Transactions: 0 Address Book: 0 ```
--- **Backwards compatibility**: command lines where a dash-prefixed argument follows a non-dash argument will now be parsed as an option (if recognized) or an error (if not). Previously such arguments were silently collected as positional args. The `--` separator can be used to pass arguments that begin with a dash as positional args.

pulls.title: [RFC] Scheduled transaction broadcast, minimal
pulls.body:
Minimal implementation for "Scheduled Transaction Broadcast" new feature.

Goal: Allow a user to submit a transaction to be broadcast later, at a specified time (block height). This can be done for convenience, or to hide the exact time of the transaction creation (for increased privacy).

Goal in this PR: Extend the `sendrawtransaction` RPC with an option to schedule the broadcast at a later time, determined by the lock time of the transaction.

Use case details, with the limitations of the current changeset:
- `sendrawtransaction` has an optional parameter, `delay_after_lock_time`
- If `delay_after_lock_time` is set to 0, the `nLockTime` of the transaction determines the scheduled broadcast time (in the future).
- If `delay_after_lock_time` is set to a positive number, the broadcast time will be the sum of the transaction `nLockTime` and the parameter value.
- Only height-based lock times are supported, time-based can be added later.
- Scheduled broadcast is only supported with private broadcast.
- What is a typical delay time? 3-12 blocks. (Too long times can get problematic: risk fee increase, node restart.)
- Pending transactions are NOT persisted, so pending transactions will be lost during a node stop/restart/crash (can be added later).
- Validation should happen at both submission time and broadcast time, but now this is not true, see below.
- If the goal is to conceal the real transaction creation time, the user should add a relatively short, random period to the current time (e.g between 3-12 blocks).
- No special handling for sudden fee increase situations.
- Pending (submitted but not yet broadcast) transactions can be inspected via existing `getprivatebroadcastinfo` RPC.
- The (pre-existing) `abortprivatebroadcast` RPC can be used to cancel a pending transaction submission.
- No special support from the wallet subsystem. (A submitted but not broadcast transactions is not visible in the wallet.)
- It is possible intentionally set the locktime of a TX in the past (e.g. as a measure against wallet fingerprinting), and still use a later schedule time -- `delay_after_lock_time` with a positive value can be used to distance the submission time from the lock time.

Solution Details:
- The solution is based on the Private Broadcast implementation. 
- Transactions are stored in the already-existing `m_transactions` collection.
- A scheduled periodic check is added to check for transactions that have became due. The implementation is very similar to the existing retry logic (`ReattemptPrivateBroadcast`). Alternative: triggered by new blocks.
- Queue is not persisted currently, to be added later.
- Submit-time validation is skipped, as it would fail, due to the future locktime. To be added later.

Further improvements:
- Add a cap on the time lock, on how far in the future it is acceptable, e.g. max 7 days / 1008 blocks.
- Support time-based locktime as well. Interpret `delay_after_lock_time` in _10-minute_ units if time-based lock is used.
- At submission time, perform validation but without timelock checks. This requires a small validation change (add bypass timelocks options to methods `ProcessTransaction` and `AcceptToMemoryPool`).
- Persist the queue with pending broadcasts, so scheduled broadcasts survive node restarts.

Related issue: #34118

pulls.title: http: support unix sockets
pulls.body:
Closes https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/5029

Accept unix socket paths as options for `-rpcbind=` (server) and `-rpcconnect=` (bitcoin-cli). Options follow the same pattern as `ipcbind`:

- `=unix` is a magic keyword that means `<datadir>/http.sock`
- `=unix:relative/path` means `<datadir>/relative/path`
- `=unix:/absolute/path` means `/absolute/path`

We delete any existing `http.sock` before calling `bind()` and do not clean up at shutdown.

Because access is handled by the filesystem, `-rpcallowip` is ignored for unix sockets and not required at all if we are *only* binding to unix sockets.

Authentication by username/password/cookie is still required.

A new option `--httpunix` is added to the test framework and added to test_runner for `rpc_bind.py` and `interface_http.py` for CI, but (like `--usecli`) most other tests should also pass with that option. When set, bitcoind is started with `-rpcbind=unix...`which overrides `tcp://localhost` entirely. `AuthProxy` has been extended to connect directly to the unix socket.

Try it out!
```
bitcoind -regtest -rpcbind=unix
bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcconnect=unix getbestblockhash
```

Refactored code:

Back in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/27375 we added unix socket support but it was isolated to the `Proxy` class. That created a bit of tech debt which we pay off in this PR. Two new classes are implemented:
- `UnixSocketAddr` reflects the `CService` API for generic unix sockets, without bitcoin-p2p-specific attributes
- `SocketAddr` holds a variant of `UnixSocketAddr` and `Cservice` so classes like `Proxy` and `HTTPServer` can operate on an abstract level, with either socket type.
- `CNetAddr` and `CService` are left untouched -- they are somewhat dirty combinations of generic socket classes and bitcoin p2p code, adding unix sockets to those classes wouldn't make sense for bitcoin p2p operations and that's why this design was chosen.

Follow-up suggestions:
- Deduplicate some of the unix socket path resolution code between IPC and HTTP
- On macos the default unix socket buffer size is only ~8k. In the functional tests we have to bump the python client socket buffer up to ~256k or the "throttle" tests will stall on macos. We could apply this socket option on the server side as well, only on macos... requires some bike shedding.
- This option replaces TCP but it does not replace HTTP, there may be a more efficient transport protocol.

pulls.title: orphanage: Fix orphan reconsideration disconnect hole, add 1p1c invariant harness
pulls.body:
The first commit adds `p2p_1p1c_liveness`, an end-to-end fuzz target for parent and child relay. It
  drives a real PeerManager with real messages and validation, and checks that if an honest peer announces
  the child of an acceptable parent and child, the child reaches the mempool within a bounded time,
  whatever other peers do. Known liveness holes are marked in the target as flags that turn the check off
  once opened, including this one. With that flag turned off, the target finds this bug on master from an
  empty corpus in under an hour on one core; an earlier version found it first
  (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36371#issuecomment-5937814761).

  The second commit hands reconsideration over to a remaining announcer when the marked announcement is
  erased, and removes the flag.

Follow-up PR to fill the holes is here: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36506
